findings.evidence: Historical relativistic mass is never promoted to speed-dependent invariant mass. The functional speed relation, total-versus-kinetic energy, and before/after-rest mass change are independently checked. A numeric endpoint coincidence does not create extra universally true options.

The own-rest-frame E0=m0c^2 definition remains true at any chosen-frame speed. The alternative total-energy expression agrees only at rest and the kinetic expression only accidentally at gamma=2; both fail the universal definition.

Heat is retained by the same resting system without matter loss, so rest energy and invariant system mass increase. This is not an assertion that individual molecular invariant masses increase with speed. Balance-resolution limits are tied to the historical source period, not every era.
Both languages specify local synchronized event-clock simultaneity and B-to-A motion. Independently tA-tB=gammaV*V*(x'A-x'B)/c^2>0; B is earlier. No flash-arrival argument is substituted.

Exact gamma=40000 gives beta=sqrt(1-6.25e-10)<1. Rationalizing 1-beta gives 3.1250000004882812501525878906846046448014676571014570072353308205523e-10. A separate offline 90-digit Decimal calculation confirmed the author's high-precision digits. Wrong alternatives imply gamma=200 and about 28284.27, not 40000.

The source omits numeric specific heat, so the draft properly uses mean cw and Delta m0=(1 kg)*mean cw*(50 K)/c^2. 323.15 K is a false absolute-temperature-offset conversion; the half-factor alternative is also false. No optional 4200 J/(kg K) or 3e8 m/s value is supplied to learners. If explicitly added, those classroom constants give about 2.3e-12 kg=2.3e-9 g, not an exact source-derived number. Numerical unavailability and added physical closure conditions are recorded honestly.

All seven complete sources are represented one-to-one per language. Selection does not demonstrate unaided formula recall, written definition/explanation, Lorentz derivation, algebraic construction or numerical evaluation. The author records these losses in limitations and coverage; none silently removes a key source distinction. Related mass-energy questions permit concept application but do not reveal a marked key or duplicate a full response task.

All visible stems and all options were manually compared across Chinese and English, including universal/conditional quantifiers, orientation, energy retention, units, constants and precision. Complete independent true sets and every author misconception were subsequently compared. No semantic mismatch, definite authoring defect or unresolved blocker was found.

manually_reviewed_pairs.evidence: Both languages specify historical m, invariant m0>0, speed domain 0<=v<c, and identical reciprocal/square-root formula alternatives. The same domain-wide, rather than endpoint-only, identity is requested.

Both languages define E total, E0 rest, K=E-E0, and historical m versus invariant m0. Both c options impose rest before and after; both d options keep internal state fixed while overall speed changes. 'All correct' and multiple mode agree.

Both request the rest-energy definition across different/any chosen-frame speeds and contrast kinetic energy, chosen-frame total energy and own-rest-frame energy with identical gamma formulas. Neither translation loses the universal-speed qualifier.

Both retain the same body at rest before/after, no matter loss, all Q>0 retained internally, and ordinary source-era measurement capabilities. The English stem's 'capabilities discussed in the source' and b's 'balances of that period' match the explicit Chinese historical scope, not a universal ban on measurement.

Both say the train moves from rear B toward front A; synchronized local train clocks assign equal strike times, explicitly not flash-reception times; both ask ground local-clock order and offer A-first/B-first/same-time in the same order.
Both use historical relativistic m=40000*m0 with invariant m0 and ask an exact speed expression in c. All three formulas and the distinction between 40000 and 40000^2 are identical.

Both retain 1 kg and a 50 deg C rise, explicitly add rest/no-loss/no-phase-change/retained-heat/negligible-work conditions, define positive mean specific heat over the interval in J/(kg K), and state its number is not supplied. 323.15 K, 50 K, and the factor 2 appear identically in the options. Neither version adds optional standard constants.
